originBelt: Mithila / Terai Wetland Ponds & Artisanal Popping Hubs
whatItIs: NaturesMud Makhana (Fox Nuts) are hand-graded, large-size puffed lotus seeds (Euryale ferox) harvested from clean wetland ponds in the Mithila/Terai belt and traditionally popped over earthen ovens. Naturally low in fat and rich in plant protein, calcium, and phosphorus, our 50 GM jar contains crisp, unbleached whole puffs with zero palm oil, zero artificial seasoning, and zero preservatives.
nepaliKitchenUses: 5-Minute Ghee-Roasted Evening Snack: Dry-roast a handful of Makhana in a pan with 1/2 teaspoon of cow ghee or Virgin Coconut Oil, a pinch of turmeric, and Himalayan Black Salt (Bire Noon) until crisp.

Homemade Baby Makhana Powder (6M+): Dry-roast plain Makhana until brittle, cool completely, and grind in a mixer to make a calcium-rich powder for baby lito/kheer (from 6 months, as advised by your pediatrician).
Festive Makhana Kheer (Fast / Vrat Recipe): Simmer crushed roasted Makhana in milk with chopped Cashews, Almonds, and Dates Powder for Navratri, Teej, or Ekadashi fasting.
Matar-Makhana Tarkari: Add toasted Makhana to green pea and tomato gravy for a festive Nepali dinner curry.
whoItSuits: Loved by health-conscious office snackers replacing fried chips and Kurkure, fasting (vrat) observers, elders needing a light evening snack, and parents grinding homemade makhana cereal for babies (from 6 months, as advised by your pediatrician).
monsoonStorage: Puffed lotus seeds lose their crunch quickly if left exposed to humid air. Keep the jar tightly closed at all times; if the puffs ever absorb monsoon moisture, simply dry-roast them in a pan for 2–3 minutes to restore 100% crispness.

faqs.q: What is the price of Makhana (मखाना / Fox Nuts) in Nepal?
faqs.a: NaturesMud Makhana (Fox Nuts) 50 GM jar is priced at Rs. 390 in Nepal (equivalent to Rs. 780 per 100g). Because puffed lotus seeds are ultra-lightweight like popcorn, 50 GM fills a full jar.

faqs.q: Can I eat Makhana straight from the jar or should I roast it?
faqs.a: You can eat them straight, but dry-roasting Makhana in a pan on low heat for 3–4 minutes (with or without a drop of ghee/coconut oil and Pink Salt) makes them extra crunchy and nutty.

faqs.q: How do I make Makhana lito for a 6-month+ baby?
faqs.a: Dry-roast Makhana on low heat until crisp, let cool, grind into a fine powder, and cook 1–2 teaspoons in water or milk for 3 minutes (suitable from 6 months, as advised by your pediatrician).

faqs.q: Why is a 50 GM jar of Makhana so large in volume?
faqs.a: Makhana is a puffed seed filled with air pockets, so 50 GM by weight has the same volume as 200 GM–250 GM of dense nuts like almonds or cashews.

faqs.q: Is Makhana suitable for Ekadashi, Teej, and Navratri fasting (व्रत)?
faqs.a: Yes, Makhana is a non-cereal aquatic seed traditionally eaten during Hindu fasting days (vrat) roasted in pure ghee with Sendha/Pink Salt or cooked as Makhana Kheer.
